Only on the 2010 list; do not use without further verification.

name: Ghisulal Rathod
current_role: Founder, Cello group; former non-executive chairman of Wim Plast Ltd (1988-2020)
profile: Ghisulal Dhanraj Rathod founded the Mumbai-based Cello plastics group, starting with plastic bangles and PVC footwear in Goregaon before building the Cello brand of housewares, writing instruments and furniture; Wim Plast (Cello moulded furniture) was a listed group company. The business is now run by his sons Pradeep and Pankaj and grandson Gaurav via Cello World Ltd (listed 2023).
interesting_fact: Cello started in 1967 with seven machines and about sixty workers making plastic bangles and PVC footwear in Goregaon, Mumbai, and grew into one of India's best-known consumerware brands.
deep_cut_fact: After seeing American households store food in round plastic containers on a US trip, he launched insulated casseroles in India in the late 1980s, a product that became a Cello staple.
notes: Patriarch, likely elderly and not public-facing; sources differ on founding dates (1962/1967/1974). Day-to-day leadership is son Pradeep Rathod (CMD, Cello World), the more practical outreach target. Reports say Wim Plast was being merged into Cello Consumer Products (2026, unverified).

name: Sonal Yatin Kakodkar
current_role: Listed shareholder/family member associated with Parle Products (per Hurun India 2018-2019); no public executive role found
profile: Appears on Hurun India 2018-2019 (about US$132m) with wealth attributed to Parle Products, the Mumbai biscuit maker (Parle-G) founded in 1929 and controlled by the Chauhan family. No public biography, interviews or executive role were found; she appears to be a passive family shareholder.
interesting_fact: Parle Products, the source of her listed wealth, became India's first packaged-food company to pass US$2bn in annual revenue (FY22).
notes: Very private; family relationship to the Parle Products Chauhans not publicly documented. Not a public-facing figure; only route is via Parle Products corporate.

name: Zhang Zhongquan

name: Girish Saligram
current_role: President, CEO and Director, Weatherford International plc (NASDAQ: WFRD), Houston
profile: Engineer-turned-oilfield-services executive who has run Weatherford since October 2020, leading its post-bankruptcy turnaround and return to profitability. Previously COO of Exterran (from 2016) and spent about 20 years at GE, in GE Healthcare and later GE Oil & Gas. His wealth comes largely from Weatherford equity awards.
interesting_fact: He spent roughly 12 years at GE Healthcare in engineering, services and operations before moving into oil and gas, an unusual route into the CEO seat of a major oilfield services firm.
deep_cut_fact: Before Exterran he ran GE Oil & Gas's Contractual Services business from Florence, Italy; he holds an engineering degree from Bangalore University, an MS in computer science and a Kellogg MBA.
notes: Frequent energy-conference speaker (ADIPEC, CERAWeek-type events); writes occasionally for SPE's JPT. Good fit for an energy podcast; route via Weatherford corporate communications (media contact Kelley Hughes per releases).

name: Reena Kamalkumar Agrawal
current_role: Family shareholder associated with Haldiram's Nagpur business (per Hurun India 2018-2019); no public executive role found
profile: Listed on Hurun India 2018-2019 (about US$120m) with wealth from Haldiram Foods International, the Nagpur arm of the Haldiram's snacks group built by Shivkisan Agrawal. Her name suggests a link to executive director Kamalkumar Agrawal, but no public source confirms her role. The Nagpur and Delhi FMCG businesses merged in 2025 into Haldiram Snacks Food Pvt Ltd.
interesting_fact: Haldiram's began as a small sweet shop in Bikaner; the Nagpur and Delhi family branches completed a merger in 2025 to form Haldiram Snacks Food Pvt Ltd, one of India's largest packaged-snack companies.
notes: Very private, no public profile found; relationship to Kamal Agrawal inferred from the patronymic only and unconfirmed. Outreach would go via Haldiram's corporate; Kamal Agrawal is the more visible family member.

name: Ravi Sanghi
current_role: Former Chairman & MD, Sanghi Industries Ltd (until Dec 2023); director, Sanghi SEZ Pvt Ltd
profile: Hyderabad-based promoter who led Sanghi Industries from non-cement products (1985) into cement in 2003, building a large integrated plant on one of India's biggest limestone reserves in Kutch, Gujarat. In August 2023 he and his family sold control to Adani's Ambuja Cements at an enterprise value of about Rs 5,000 crore; he stepped down as CMD in December 2023 and remains a director of Sanghi SEZ.
interesting_fact: At the Ambuja sale he highlighted the Kutch site's potential to become the world's largest clinker manufacturing complex; the plant had 6.6 MTPA clinker and 6.1 MTPA grinding capacity.
deep_cut_fact: Sanghi Industries built its own captive port at Sanghipuram in Kutch to move cement and clinker by sea, an asset Adani later planned to expand to handle larger ships.
notes: Post-exit; no personal website or verified social accounts found. Sanghi Industries is now Adani/Ambuja-controlled, so company IR is not a route to him. Family also linked to Sanghi Polyesters (Hyderabad).

name: David Hallal
current_role: Chairman (since 2017) and CEO (since April 2025), Scholar Rock Holding Corp (NASDAQ: SRRK); Executive Chairman, ElevateBio
profile: Biotech commercial executive who spent 2006-2016 at Alexion Pharmaceuticals, rising from Chief Commercial Officer to COO and CEO, then co-founded/led cell and gene therapy company ElevateBio. He chaired Scholar Rock's board from 2017 and took over as CEO in 2025 to bring its SMA drug apitegromab to market; his wealth comes largely from Scholar Rock equity.
interesting_fact: He built Alexion's commercial infrastructure for Soliris, one of the world's most expensive drugs for ultra-rare diseases, before becoming the company's CEO.
deep_cut_fact: A psychology graduate of the University of New Hampshire, he began his career in 1988 at The Upjohn Company, and as VP of Sales at OSI Eyetech led the US launch of Macugen; he still sits on the UNH Foundation board.
notes: Also chairs Kalaris Therapeutics; listed as iTeos director in SEC data. Biotech rather than energy, so a stretch for the podcast's theme; route via Scholar Rock media (Molly MacLeod per releases).

name: Fred Burke
current_role: President, CEO and co-founder, Guardian Pharmacy Services, Inc. (NYSE: GRDN), Atlanta
profile: Serial Atlanta healthcare entrepreneur who co-founded nuclear pharmacy business Central Pharmacy Services (1992-2001, sold to Cardinal Health) and then, in 2003-04, Guardian Pharmacy, which grew by partnering with local long-term-care pharmacies into a national network serving assisted-living and senior-care facilities. Guardian IPO'd on the NYSE in 2024; his wealth is mainly Guardian stock.
interesting_fact: He co-founded the Senior Care Pharmacy Coalition, the only Washington-based group exclusively representing independent long-term-care pharmacies, and later served as its chairman.
deep_cut_fact: Before healthcare he was a US Air Force communications officer leading a combat communications unit, a Procter & Gamble brand manager, and a McKinsey consultant in Atlanta and Brussels; he holds an engineering BS from Mississippi State and an MS from Purdue's Krannert School.
notes: Still CEO as of June 2026 leadership changes (COO/CFO reshuffle, co-founder Kendall Forbes retiring). Healthcare services rather than energy; IR contact is Ashley Stockton per releases. IR email seen in multiple press releases via search; site renders it obfuscated.

name: David Kroin
current_role: Founder and Chief Investment Officer, Deep Track Capital (Greenwich, CT)
profile: Life-sciences hedge fund manager with 25+ years in healthcare investing. He co-founded Great Point Partners in 2003, co-managing its long/short biotech fund, then launched Deep Track Capital (c. 2020-21), which reported about US$5bn in assets in 2024. Deep Track's 10%+ stakes in companies such as Dynavax, LB Pharmaceuticals and Attovia account for his SEC insider listing.
interesting_fact: Deep Track grew to manage roughly US$5.1bn in discretionary assets (Form ADV, March 2024) within a few years of launch, investing only in life sciences.
deep_cut_fact: He trained as an actuary, earning a BS in Actuarial Mathematics from the University of Michigan, and serves on the leadership council of Michigan's Life Sciences Institute.
notes: Low public profile; no interviews or social accounts found. Deep-cut source is an investor-profile aggregator (mirrors firm bio); verify before use. Biotech investor, limited fit for an energy/data-center theme.

name: Jeffrey Stoops
current_role: Chair of the Board, SBA Communications Corp (NASDAQ: SBAC), since January 2024
profile: Florida corporate/M&A lawyer who joined wireless tower company SBA Communications in 1997, served as CFO, President (2000) and CEO (2002-2023), turning it into one of the world's largest independent tower owners across the Americas and beyond. He retired as CEO in December 2023 and now chairs SBA's board; he co-founded the Stoops Family Foundation (health and education).
interesting_fact: He was brought into SBA in 1997 specifically to transition it from a tower-site services firm into a tower owner, an asset-based model that became the core of the business.
deep_cut_fact: An FSU College of Law grad (1984), he spent 13 years as a corporate/M&A lawyer at Gunster Yoakley; his first big task at SBA was raising its initial US$30m private placement. His motto: 'To get rewards in life, you have to take some risks.'
notes: Good fit for a digital-infrastructure angle (towers, fiber, edge data centers). Based in Boca Raton area; FSU donor (law school, social work, Seminole Boosters). Route via SBA media relations.

name: Robert L Bugbee
current_role: President and Director, Scorpio Tankers Inc. (NYSE: STNG) and the Scorpio group
profile: British-born shipping executive who has run Scorpio Tankers, one of the world's largest product-tanker fleets, since its 2010 IPO alongside the Lolli-Ghetti family's Scorpio group. Earlier he spent 1995-2007 at OMI Corporation, rising to President until its sale, and co-founded Eneti (offshore wind installation vessels, 2013-2022). His wealth stems largely from Scorpio Tankers equity.
interesting_fact: He co-founded and ran Eneti Inc., which pivoted from dry-bulk shipping into building offshore wind-turbine installation vessels, a direct link between tanker shipping and the energy transition.
deep_cut_fact: He began his shipping career in 1984 at Gotaas-Larsen Shipping Corporation and holds a University of London degree; between OMI and Scorpio he was briefly a partner at commodities investor Ospraie Management (2007-08).
notes: Outspoken on tanker/oil markets and a regular at Capital Link and TradeWinds forums; strong energy-shipping angle. IR head James Doyle is the named contact.

name: Anat Ashkenazi
current_role: SVP and Chief Financial Officer, Alphabet Inc. and Google (since July 2024)
profile: Israeli-American finance executive who spent 23 years at Eli Lilly, rising to CFO (2021-2024) during the Mounjaro/Zepbound GLP-1 boom, before succeeding Ruth Porat as Alphabet's CFO in 2024. She now oversees one of tech's largest capital programs, with roughly US$91bn of 2025 capex aimed largely at AI infrastructure. Her wealth is mostly Alphabet stock awards.
interesting_fact: Fortune ranked her No. 48 on its 2026 Most Powerful Women list, citing Alphabet's AI capex program, one of the most aggressive capital deployments in tech history.
deep_cut_fact: Before moving to Lilly in 2001 she worked in Israel's financial sector, including at credit-rating agency Ma'alot Standard & Poor's and Bank Hapoalim; she studied at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem and earned an MBA from Tel Aviv University.
notes: Highly relevant to data-center/energy theme (Alphabet AI capex, power procurement), but very hard to book; route only via Google corporate communications.

name: Matthew Alty
current_role: President, Lyntris Inc. (NASDAQ: LYNX); Director, Karman Holdings (KRMN)
profile: Aerospace and defense manufacturing executive who, as CEO of Vitesse Systems, grew it by acquisition into a maker of antennas, thermal management and defense hardware. Vitesse combined with Accelint to form defense-tech company Lyntris (sensing, AI data fusion, C2), where he is President. Earlier he was COO of Valence Surface Technologies and a VP at Bodycote.
interesting_fact: At Valence Surface Technologies he led the integration of nine acquisitions to create North America's largest aerospace-accredited surface-finishing business.
deep_cut_fact: He is a trained metallurgist, with a BSc in Metallurgy and Materials Science from the University of Liverpool (plus an MBA from Loyola Marymount), and earlier ran Bodycote's global surface technology business across 11 sites in five countries.
notes: Company account on X, not personal. Defense-tech angle rather than energy. Web-search budget ran out during this lane; profile built from the Lyntris site only.

name: Rodrigo Cardoso Barbosa
current_role: President and CEO, Aura Minerals Inc. (Nasdaq: AUGO; TSX: ORA; B3)
profile: Brazilian mechanical engineer who leads Aura Minerals, a mid-tier gold and copper producer with mines and projects across Brazil, Mexico, Honduras, Guatemala and Colombia (Almas, Borborema, Aranzazu, Minosa, Era Dorada, Serra Grande). Under his leadership Aura added a Nasdaq listing alongside TSX and B3; his wealth is mainly Aura equity.
interesting_fact: Aura is one of the few miners listed on three exchanges at once (Nasdaq, Toronto and Brazil's B3) and has become a Russell 1000 component.

name: John P Rielly
current_role: Former EVP and CFO, Hess Corporation (CFO 2004-2025); current role after the July 2025 Chevron-Hess merger not confirmed
profile: Accountant-turned-energy CFO who joined Hess in 2001 as VP and Controller and served as CFO from 2004 (EVP from 2020) through Hess's growth into a major Guyana (Stabroek) and Bakken producer and its acquisition by Chevron, completed in 2025. Before Hess he spent 17 years at Ernst & Young, becoming a partner. His wealth stems from Hess equity converted in the merger.
interesting_fact: He was Hess's CFO for over two decades, spanning the company's transformation from an integrated refiner/marketer into a pure-play E&P anchored by the Stabroek discovery offshore Guyana and its eventual sale to Chevron.
deep_cut_fact: Before joining Hess in 2001 he spent 17 years at Ernst & Young, rising to partner, and his first Hess role was Vice President and Controller (2001-2004).
notes: Hess is now a Chevron subsidiary (merger completed 2025), so former Hess IR channels are defunct; no personal site or social accounts found. Web-search budget ran out, so post-merger role (e.g. any board seats) unverified. Strong energy-finance perspective for the podcast.

name: Ronan Harris
current_role: Chief Commercial Officer, Snap Inc. (NYSE: SNAP), since September 2026
profile: Irish technology executive who spent 17+ years at Google, latterly as Vice President and Managing Director for the UK and Ireland, before joining Snap as President of EMEA for nearly four years. In September 2026 he became Snap's Chief Commercial Officer, overseeing its global advertising and revenue business; his wealth stems from Snap equity awards.
interesting_fact: Before Snap he spent more than 17 years at Google, running its UK and Ireland business as VP and Managing Director.
deep_cut_fact: He is an engineer by training, with a B.E. in Electronic Engineering from University College Dublin.
notes: Not to be confused with Ronan Harris of the band VNV Nation. Ad-tech/consumer social angle; limited energy fit. Web-search budget ran out, so bio is from Snap's IR page only.

name: Daniel Spence
current_role: Co-founder and major (8%+) shareholder of Paysign, Inc. (NASDAQ: PAYS); former CTO, EVP and director
profile: Payments technologist who co-founded 3PEA Technologies (now Paysign, Henderson, Nevada) with Mark Newcomer in 2001 and designed the architecture of the Paysign prepaid-card and payments platform, serving as CTO until 2020 and a director from 2006. He no longer appears as an officer or director but remains one of the largest individual shareholders.
interesting_fact: He personally designed the architecture of the PaySign payments platform, which grew from a two-founder startup into a Nasdaq-listed prepaid card and pharma co-pay processor.
deep_cut_fact: Before fintech he spent a decade (1984-94) at Coca-Cola in Australia building financial systems for its worldwide operations, then was Director of Technology Planning at The Associated Press (1997-99), and later managed ANZ Bank's Medicare Easyclaim rollout in Australia.
notes: Very low public profile; no longer in management, so company channels may not reach him. Strong Australia connection. Alive status not independently confirmed (still filing Form 4s in 2025).

name: Bill W Wheat
current_role: Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer, D.R. Horton, Inc. (NYSE: DHI), since 2003
profile: Career finance executive who joined D.R. Horton, America's largest homebuilder by volume, in 1998 as an accounting manager and rose to Controller (2000) and CFO (2003); he also sat on the board from 2003 to 2011. He has steered the Arlington, Texas company's finances through the housing crash and its subsequent growth; his wealth comes from long-held D.R. Horton equity.
interesting_fact: He has been CFO of D.R. Horton, the largest US homebuilder by volume, continuously since 2003 - more than two decades in the role - and earlier also served on its board (2003-2011).
deep_cut_fact: He joined D.R. Horton in 1998 as an accounting manager after stints at Price Waterhouse and home-furnishings retailer The Bombay Company; he is a 1988 Baylor University BBA in accounting and finance.
notes: Low-profile CFO; regular voice on DHI earnings calls. Homebuilding rather than energy.

name: Gonzalo M Avendano
current_role: Independent Director, Intrepid Potash, Inc. (NYSE: IPI), since January 2025; Investment Advisor, Clearway Capital Management
profile: Lawyer (University of Buenos Aires) turned wealth manager with 30+ years at Lehman Brothers, Deutsche Bank and UBS, then founder of Silver Mills (2005-14). Since 2014 he has advised at Clearway Capital Management, Intrepid Potash's largest holder (~9%), and joined Intrepid's board in 2025. The insider wealth figure likely reflects Clearway holdings, not his own 3,328 shares.
interesting_fact: He sits on the board of the only US producer of muriate of potash as an adviser to its largest stockholder, Clearway Capital (about 9% of shares).
deep_cut_fact: Alongside his investment career he has owned and operated Haras Patagones SRL, a private agricultural company, since 2009; he earned his law degree at the University of Buenos Aires.
notes: Private investor with minimal public footprint; net-worth figure in the source data probably attributes Clearway's stake to him. 'Only US producer of muriate of potash' is Intrepid's own description, not re-verified this session. No published IR email found.
